questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University of Bologna is one of the best in Europe. The cultural experiences in Italy are fantastic and getting to enjoy that for many months was a great motivator.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Relatively easy. UCPH made it fairly easy to understand, though the University of Bologna website and student services could really do with a bit of an upgrade since getting any information out of them is a very long process that rarely yields any fruit.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was able to very quickly verify my having arrived via web call with the university and the instructions on how to get my student ID card that same day were incredibly quick. This made it very easy to get everything sorted out.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. Bologna is a city notorious for how difficult it is to find housing for students. I had to pay €250 to a realty agency to help me find a place that was within the budget necessary.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Come at least a month ahead of time like I did. Even then it was difficult. But try to find something online way ahead of time to save on money. It is a tough location to find housing since it is only a city of 300,000 but the university makes up a huge proportion of the population, so housing is always extensively in demand. Especially if you are not fluent in the local language.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy. You simply show your passport, plane ticket (or other mode of arrival), and your Erasmus letter on an online video chat with the university international student office and they get you set up on the spot. You then receive an email with the information to get your student ID card from a machine in one of several locations throughout the city so it is very convenient.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The UCPH office was very helpful when it came to figuring things out on the Danish end. It was less helpful in Italy, but that is likely because they get an intensive amount of Erasmus students and they have less budget and administrative capacity. So long as you come early and plan ahead I would say that most people will be fine, but it is not as seamless an experience as in Denmark.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. I had to change schedules a few times to ensure that the OLA could be approved by both Bologna and Copenhagen, but at the end of the day it was fine since I was still able to find classes that were to my liking and that both universities would approve.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend that they come early, plan ahead, and ensure that they have a conversation with UCPH ahead of time about how OLA might work with them and at other institutions. Try to call Bologna ahead of time to get an over the phone explanation of how the system works since you are not likely to get a response or anything via email unless it is one of those mass sent emails which does have information but sometimes they raise more questions than they answer.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had to take one 10 ECTS BA course because it fell under the category required by Bologna to take given the deal they have with UCPH as the credits had to fall under economics and management. The rest I was able to sort out in one way or another to get 16 ECTS under what they wanted and then another 16 ECTS of what I wanted so that the contract was split 50-50 and they would sign off on it. It is a big annoying since UCPH signed off on all the courses that I wanted and pre-approved them, but the problem was with Bologna's system and requirements that I do what they wanted to study here citing an agreement with UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Bologna has a more traditional lecture system like in both universities around the world with only one professor instead of the two professor model with course seminars in my program at UCPH. I FAR in a way prefer the way that Bologna does things since it is just more old school and what I prefer as I feel that the classes are more meaningful and there is far less fluff in the materials and no pointless group exercises that do not bring me any sort of value.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. History and international Relations of The Middle East
2. Politics of European Institutions
3. Global Connections: A Long-Term History
4. Central Banking and Monetary Policy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I recommend that they take half of their credits as required by the University of Bologna and the other half just take whatever they want that they can get pre-approval one. It is a pretty relaxed atmosphere down here so you have a ton of options in English and even other languages.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Having to pay an agency to help me find a place since it is impossible to find a place. That was a cost of €250 euros which was very expensive, but it is one of the only ways to help you find a cheap place in Bologna.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything here is far less expensive than in Denmark with the same if not greater quality. So the cost of living is definitely a lot lower which makes it more budget friendly for students. The housing is still expensive by Italian standards and especially given the EU Erasmus grant, but it is still more affordable than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Tons of things from politics to reading to history to science. I do not tend to go to stuff like that, but they are there for those that like them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Everything the city has to offer in terms of culture and culinary experiences. Bologna is a fantastic city and I highly recommend it to everyone. It is a town where you can make a ton of university friends or just relax on your own and enjoy la dolce vita. It is really up to you.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is a ton of historical things to see in the Emilia-Romagna region where Bologna is located. Cities like Modena, Parma, Ferrara, and Rimini are in the region and they are fantastic cities which beautiful architecture and histories. There is the Adriatic Sea by Rimini, and you can take a day trip to San Marino which is a country completely surrounded by Italy. Milan, Venice, Padua, and Florence are also fairly close to Bologna and easy to see in a day. And while Rome is further away you can get very cheap tickets on a bus to go see the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Extremely easy. Italians are a very welcoming people and it is a very loving culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None. I loved it here and it was far easier to get used to here than Denmark.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The hospitality. The food. The warmth and friendliness of the people. And their openmindness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Come early to find a place 
2. Keep an open mind as the culture is different from Denmark 
3. Relax and enjoy it a bit more. Do not stress as much as you would in other places. Try to let the feeling carry you since the bureaucracy is a lot to handle, but you need to take it in strides.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: NA

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to live in a place like Italy for so many months and being able to enjoy its culture in a way that I might never again get to do in my life given work and responsibilities is a memory that I will cherish forever. It was not so much the classes but everything surrounding my time living in Italy that has made it one of the most memorable experiences of my life.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sort out housing (please refer to above)

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: I encourage everyone who wants to do Erasmus to consider Italy, and Bologna in particular. You will love it here.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
